strengths: Identifies and formalizes a critical and highly prevalent failure mode, 'Marginal Path Collapse' (MPC), which occurs when composing heterogeneous generative experts with mismatched noise schedules.

Provides a theoretically rigorous framework, including a sharp sufficient Path Existence Criterion (PEC) and the Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE) sampler that generalizes Feynman–Kac steering to time-varying exponents.

Extensive and high-quality empirical validation on diverse tasks, including synthetic benchmarks, highly complex scientific tasks (flexible-pose scaffold decoration, fragment linking) where it outperforms specialized monolithic models, and compositional image generation.
Excellent presentation and writing quality. The paper is very clear, highly detailed, and the analysis of why task-specific noise schedules are necessary is incredibly insightful.
Practically minded; introduces a lightweight variant (ACE-lite) to address computational and VRAM overhead, showing strong awareness of resource constraints.
weaknesses: The selection and tuning of the bump parameters ($B_1$ and $B_2$) involve some empirical search, and excessive correction can negatively impact sample quality by deviating from the optimal transport trajectory.

The theoretical guarantees of the PEC (Theorem 2.1) are currently limited to Gaussian-prior-to-compactly-supported targets, meaning extensions to discrete, categorical, or other non-Gaussian setups are left as future work.

strengths: Identifies and formalizes a critical and previously overlooked failure mode in inference-time diffusion steering: Marginal Path Collapse (MPC), which occurs due to mismatched noise schedules or negative exponents in heterogeneous compositions.

Provides a mathematically rigorous framework, including a sharp sufficient Path Existence Criterion (PEC) and a novel sampling algorithm, Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE), which generalizes Feynman-Kac steering to time-varying exponents.
Theoretically links the magnitude of the path existence criterion to the quantile radius of the intermediate distribution, demonstrating how ACE acts as a variance reduction/concentration mechanism.

Demonstrates strong empirical performance on a challenging and realistic scientific task (flexible-pose scaffold decoration and fragment linking) by successfully composing heterogeneous de-novo, conformer, and pocket-conditioned SBDD models, outperforming specialized monolithic baselines.

Excellent presentation with clear writing, illustrative figures (such as the 2D checkerboard and molecular trajectories), and a highly detailed appendix containing comprehensive proofs and extensive experimental setups.
weaknesses: The choice of the bump function parameters ($B_1$ and $B_2$) requires some empirical tuning or analytical prescreening, and excessive correction can act as a multiplier on score/velocity fields, potentially amplifying network approximation errors.

Like other Feynman-Kac particle methods, ACE introduces non-trivial computational overhead due to the necessity of simulating multiple particles and tracking component log-densities. While the proposed 'ACE-lite' reduces this overhead, it exhibits higher variance in docking scores.

The theoretical guarantees of the Path Existence Criterion are currently restricted to Gaussian-to-compactly-supported targets under Gaussian-based interpolants, leaving extension to heavy-tailed or non-Gaussian priors to future work.

strengths: Rigorous formalization of 'Marginal Path Collapse' (MPC), addressing a crucial and previously overlooked failure mode in training-free heterogeneous diffusion steering.

Strong theoretical contributions: deriving a sharp Path Existence Criterion (PEC) for compactly supported targets and proving that the criterion controls the quantile radius of intermediate distributions to stabilize sampling.

Proposed a novel and elegant correction framework, Adaptive Path Correction with Exponents (ACE), which generalizes Feynman–Kac steering to time-varying exponents to dynamically ensure path normalizability.

Outstanding validation on realistic, complex scientific tasks (flexible-pose molecular scaffold decoration and fragment linking) using composed heterogeneous experts (EDM, GeoDiff, and DiffSBDD), demonstrating clear superiority over constant-exponent baselines.

Remarkably thorough manuscript and appendix, containing complete proofs, a comprehensive survey of noise schedules in molecular models, parameter sensitivity analyses, and additional evaluations on compositional text-to-image benchmarks.
weaknesses: The design of the bump functions to modify exponents relies on hyperparameters $B_1$ and $B_2$. Although a sensitivity analysis is provided, the manual selection of these parameters currently lacks an automated, fully adaptive tuning mechanism.

The proposed particle-based weighted sampling scheme (ACE) introduces additional computational overhead in terms of runtime and memory. While the authors propose a faster 'ACE-lite' variant, it comes with a trade-off in worst-case sampling performance.

The sharp sufficient condition in Theorem 2.1 assumes compactly supported target distributions. While this covers many practical modalities (images, physical coordinates), extending the main-text theory to general unbounded non-Gaussian distributions remains an open challenge.
